unlisted_practices: Assess and report the expected clinical impact of AI diagnostic tool errors to supplement technical performance metrics for any tool nearing clinical use.
Report the pathological nature of AI errors (entity, size, location) using standardised pathological terms and entities.
Adopt standardised terminology to classify and report the clinical impact of AI errors, by severity of patient impact or type of impact on care.
Categorise AI errors into major and minor errors using collaboratively defined standardised definitions.
Compare errors made by AI tools with those of human pathologists (the current standard of care) using standardised reporting of clinical implications.
Build high-quality pathology and clinical data collection and multidisciplinary team analysis into AI study design and tool development.
Update AI reporting guidelines such as CONSORT-AI, SPIRIT-AI and STARD-AI to require clinical assessment of AI errors.
Regulators should incorporate human-AI interaction and assessment of errors by clinical consequences into AI evaluation rather than relying on performance in artificial testing environments.
Incorporate the clinical risk of specific misclassifications into AI model training and verification to make algorithms sensitive to impact.

screen.reason: This is a perspective/recommendation paper focusing on how AI diagnostic errors in histopathology should be evaluated and governed in terms of clinical patient impact rather than technical metrics alone.
